newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UK INVESTMENT TRUST SET TO CONTROL VICENZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UK INVESTMENT TRUST SET TO CONTROL VICENZA.

text.p: A British investment trust linked to Scottish champions Glasgow Rangers is set to acquire a controlling stake in Italian serie A club Vicenza, the trust said on Tuesday.
The English National Investment Company (ENIC) has agreed with Britain's Stellican Limited to take a stake of almost 30 percent in Vicenza for 2.4 million pounds ($4 million).
ENIC has an option to boost its stake in the northern Italian club to 62 percent for a total investment of five million pounds.
Stellican last month became the first foreign owner of an Italian soccer club when it paid 22.75 billion lire ($13.4 million) in a bankruptcy court to buy Vicenza.

Bahamas-based millionaire financier Joe Lewis is one of the backers of ENIC. Lewis took a 25 percent stake in Rangers earlier this year and ENIC now has an option to acquire that stake for 40 million pounds.
The deal unveiled on Tuesday will leave Italian Cup holders Vicenza jointly owned by ENIC, Stellican affiliate Estimator Limited, CSI Limited and Pangolin International Limited.
Estimator is owned by Stellican founder and managing director Stephen Julius. The other two companies involved have strong ties to the international media world.
Vicenza will play in the Euopean Cup Winners' Cup next season after winning their domestic cup, the first major trophy in their 95-year history.

Vicenza have a modest history but Paolo Rossi and Roberto Baggio, Italian World Cup heroes in 1982 and 1994 respectively, played for the northern Italian club in the early stages of their careers. ($ = 0.600 British Pounds) ($ = 1700 Italian Lire)
